citation: The Daily Inter Ocean (Chicago), 1887, a notice of the Robert Law house, 838 (later 1620) Prairie Avenue, calling it 'commodious, olive green in color'; quoted on chicagology.com's 1620 S. Prairie page.
author: unsigned
locator: the phrase 'commodious, olive green in color', as the Prairie library records chicagology's quotation of it (image a16-cgy-landowner-1874-1620-law, its notes; chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/images/stream-1600-1700.json); the issue's day and page are not known here
rights_note: The Inter Ocean, 1887: a United States imprint long out of copyright.
access_notes: READ THROUGH A QUOTATION, NOT AT THE PAGE. This project has not retrieved the Inter Ocean; the four words read are chicagology's quotation, as the Prairie library's research fetch of chicagology's 1620 page (2026-10-02) recorded them. chicagology.com is not reachable from the build containers, so the page has not been re-read here (T-2476). `verified` stays false until someone opens the newspaper.
note: The only record of the house's colour: the 1874 Land Owner engraving (land_owner_1874_05_homes_of_chicago_1620_law) is monochrome and Robinson 1886 plate 10 colours it as brick. A brick house called olive green was painted over its brick, the 1870s fashion; the shade the words name is not measured.
